answer: Comet-paced issuance windows. Each new identity must wait one randomized interval (drawn from a heavy-tailed schedule) before its first outbound action is relayed, and only relayed traffic counts toward eligibility. Honest agents idle briefly; attackers running thousands of fresh identities must hold them open simultaneously through the full window, paying compute and connection costs per identity. The schedule’s saffron-tagged epochs enforce staggered admission. Any burst of ivory-clean, zero-history keys arriving together gets queued last.
